narrative:
The model determined that you have a 41% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability crossed the threshold the bank uses for approval, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were your credit history, the status of your checking account, and the level of savings you have. Your credit history actually worked in your favor: having a record that includes critical or other existing credits is more common among approved applicants and pushed the prediction toward approval. Unfortunately, the other two factors pulled strongly in the opposite direction. Your checking account currently sits in the 0-200 DM range, a situation shared by only 18% of approved borrowers, and this signaled higher risk to the model. Even more influential was your savings balance of less than 100 DM, which is the most frequent but also the weakest savings category among those who ultimately get loans.

Taken together, these signals led the bank to decide the overall risk was too high. To improve your chances next time, focus on building your savings above 100 DM and, if possible, moving your checking balance into a stronger positive range. Demonstrating steady, on-time management of existing credit obligations will also help shift future predictions in a positive direction.
